tour.title: Where the application starts
tour.description: `src/index.tsx` mounts the app and `src/App.tsx` sets up providers and the router. `src/AdminApp.tsx` is the authenticated shell, and `src/pages/lazyPages.ts` is the single registry of code-split routes. Read these first: every route you will later touch is referenced here.

tour.title: Configuration and environment
tour.description: `src/appConfig.ts` resolves the backend base URLs and a few endpoint switches; `.env.example` lists the runtime variables (Keycloak URL, realm and client id, API and app URL, cookie domain and secure flag). `vite.config.ts` wires the dev server. Knowing these prevents most local-setup confusion.

tour.title: How a request reaches the backend
tour.description: All HTTP traffic goes through `src/api/fetchData.ts`, which builds the URL, attaches auth and CSRF, and throws `FetchErrorWithOptions`. `src/utils/extractApiErrorMessage.ts` turns those errors into user-facing text and `src/utils/parseHalResponse.ts` unwraps HAL payloads. Learn this trio before writing any new API function.

tour.title: Login, tokens and the auth BFF
tour.description: `src/api/auth/auth.ts` bootstraps the session and keeps refresh timers running. Tokens live in cookies, local storage or memory depending on configuration. The cookies themselves are set by a small Node backend-for-frontend, `scripts/auth-bff-handlers.mjs`, which talks to Keycloak; `vite.authBffPlugin.ts` mounts it during development.

tour.title: Roles become UI permissions
tour.description: `src/constants/userRolesToPermissions.ts` maps Keycloak roles to permissions, merges them and applies the restricted-agency-admin ceiling. `src/hooks/useUserPermission.ts` is what components ask, and `src/utils/adminPortalAccess.ts` decides who may enter the portal at all. Nearly every 'why is this hidden?' question ends here.

tour.title: The page shell and navigation
tour.description: `src/components/Layout/Initialization.tsx` loads the user, tenant and feature data once after login. `ProtectedPageLayoutWrapper.tsx` renders the authenticated frame, `adminNavItems.ts` defines the sidebar entries and `AdminMobileNav.tsx` is the mobile counterpart. Adding a page means touching the nav items too.

tour.title: Tenant administration, the largest domain
tour.description: `src/pages/Tenants/Edit/index.tsx` is a tab host; the real content lives in `src/components/Tenants`. Start with GeneralSettings (name, logo, colours) and the ThemeBuilder, which writes the tenant's Material 3 scheme. This is the pattern the other tenant tabs follow.

tour.title: Agency and department editing
tour.description: `src/pages/Agency/Edit/index.tsx` composes GeneralInformation, RegistrationSettings (with post-code ranges) and DepartmentDetails. `src/api/agency/updateAgencyData.ts` and `departmentDetails.ts` are the write paths, and `agencySort.ts` shows how the list is ordered — a good example of pure logic extracted from a page.

tour.title: One table for every kind of user
tour.description: Consultants, agency admins, tenant admins and platform admins share `UserManagementTable.tsx`; the visible columns come from `useUserTableColumns.tsx` and the per-cohort configuration from `userTableConfigs.ts`. `src/pages/users/Edit/index.tsx` is the corresponding editor. Read the configs before adding a column.

tour.title: Invites: composer, CSV import, progress board
tour.description: `src/api/accountInvites/accountInvites.ts` exposes the whole invite lifecycle (create, send, resend, revoke, email templates). The UI is the composer, a CSV bulk path (`parseInviteCsv.ts`) and a progress board whose phase model is the pure `derivePhases.ts` — the best-tested logic file in the repo.

tour.title: The DPA gate: why the UI can be blocked
tour.description: Before a tenant's data processing agreement is signed, `DpaBlockerGate.tsx` blocks the admin area based on `getDpaGate.ts` and the predicate in `dpaBlockerGate.ts`. The admin can sign in place or forward the signing to an authorised person through `dpaForward.ts`, which also enforces a forward budget.

tour.title: Legal texts, consent and DPIA
tour.description: `LegalSettings/index.tsx` edits tenant and agency legal texts with drafts, version selection and consent-placeholder validation; publishing may trigger machine translation via `src/api/tenant/translation.ts`. The DPIA lives next door in `DpiaSettings` with its own sections and text gateway.

tour.title: Statistics as pure data shaping
tour.description: `src/pages/Statistic.tsx` is thin on purpose: `statisticDashboardData.ts` builds week starts, topic series and target statistics from the raw response of `getDashboardStatistics.ts`, and `statisticPreferences.ts` remembers the filters. Change the maths in the data module, not in the page.

tour.title: Design system, MUI migration and tests
tour.description: New form controls come from `src/components/mui/MuiFormField`; `docs/admin-mui9-antd-inventory.md` records what is still AntD. Theming flows from `themeSeeds.ts` through `useAdminTheme.hook.ts`. Tests run on Vitest with the setup in `src/test/setup.ts`, which is why AntD notices need explicit cleanup.
